step1_analysis.description: This is a lumped-element equivalent circuit of a passive balun or transformer, likely used in the RF transmitter for single-ended to differential conversion (or vice versa). It consists entirely of passive components (inductors, capacitors, resistors) representing the physical layout parasitics and coupling.

paper_reference.title: SiGe W-CDMA Transmitter for Mobile Terminal Application

Insertion_Loss.description: Signal loss from the single-ended input to each of the differential outputs.

sky130_expected.calculation: An ideal balun splits power equally, resulting in a -3dB insertion loss per branch. Parasitic resistance and substrate losses typically add 1-3dB of loss.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Standard passive balun performance at RF frequencies (e.g., 2 GHz for W-CDMA).

Amplitude_Imbalance.description: The difference in magnitude between the two differential output branches.

sky130_expected.calculation: Magnitude of output 1 (dB) minus Magnitude of output 2 (dB).
sky130_expected.reasoning: A well-designed balun should have minimal amplitude imbalance to ensure good common-mode rejection in the connected differential circuits.

Phase_Difference.description: The phase difference between the two differential output branches.

sky130_expected.calculation: Phase of output 1 minus Phase of output 2.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Ideal differential signals are exactly 180 degrees out of phase. Parasitic mismatches cause slight deviations.

step3_testbench.description: AC analysis to measure the insertion loss, amplitude imbalance, and phase difference of the passive balun at the W-CDMA operating frequency (2 GHz).
